match_note: First-round comments cite text and figures that are all in arXiv v1. Examples: the p4 quote 'Spin detection and manipulation of 4f-electron systems by a non-dissipative force...'; the 'controlling the spin by manipulating the adsorption-site symmetry' sentence; the 'bidirectional spin switching rules out exchange forces' statement; the 'more spatially localized' claim tied to Fig. 4c; Fig. 4 panels (a) and (b) both being telegraph traces; the 120 mV / 200 µV preparation protocol; A = 65 pm given only in the Fig. 1c caption; the SI Stevens parameters. Material the authors added in revision is absent from v1: Fig. 1b inset, Fig. S10d histogram, Fig. S14 (1 T/8 T calculations and 8 T data), Fig. S15a. One wording difference: v1 describes the Ho 5d/6s–Co 3d inter-atomic coupling as ferromagnetic, while the rebuttal's added text calls it antiferromagnetic.

concerns.quote: The reversible switching clearly supported that z_tip dependent exchange force is not the major driving force of the switching... I believe the discussion on the driving force of the switching should be improved.
concerns.summary: The proposed driving mechanism of the switching (strain-induced state mixing via site change) is not argued convincingly and should be stated firmly throughout.

concerns.quote: Here, the FM mode operation at a "contact" regime and the relevance between Delta_f and tip-sample interaction is not intuitively understandable.
concerns.summary: The paper should explain how frequency shift relates to tip-sample force when FM-AFM is operated in the contact (z < 0) regime.

concerns.quote: A questionable point to me is that the authors are sure to exclude the influence of the tunneling electrons on the switching in the z regime (< 0) and bias voltage of 0.2 mV
concerns.summary: Tunneling electrons at point-contact quantum conductance could cause the switching, and this has not been convincingly excluded.

concerns.quote: the authors doesn't have to rely on the previous works but can give a detailed discussion on the specific case in this work (Co tip and Ho_top atom)
concerns.summary: The ferromagnetic-to-antiferromagnetic crossover in the tip-Ho exchange force is not explained physically for this specific Co-Ho system (R1 frames this as major, R2 as a minor clarification).

concerns.quote: Superparamagnetic nature of a magnetic tip apex has been thoroughly studied in the works [Appl. Phys. Lett. 103, 032407 (2013)] and [Nano Convergence 4, 8 (2017)]
concerns.summary: Prior work on superparamagnetic tip apexes should be cited.

concerns.quote: A clear example of "controlling the spin by manipulating the adsorption-site symmetry" (page 4, lines 158-159) has been recently published
concerns.summary: A recent publication demonstrating spin control via adsorption-site symmetry should be cited.

concerns.quote: How about using an inset just for the two states of the interest using an energy scale, comparable to the Zeeman energy splitting of the states?
concerns.summary: Fig. 1b cannot show the Zeeman splitting of the two ground states at its ~300 meV scale, so a zoomed inset is suggested.

concerns.quote: the manuscript does not convincingly demonstrate that mechanical readout and writing provide a clear conceptual or practical advantage over electrical reading and writing schemes (as in Ref. 5).
concerns.summary: It is unclear that force-based read/write offers a significant advance over established current-based STM schemes.

concerns.quote: The force-based readout requires probing times of several seconds to tens of seconds due to the slow tip approach, whereas electrical readout based on tunnel current in STM-based schemes can be performed on much shorter timescales.
concerns.summary: Slow force-based readout limits practical relevance, and a faster tip approach might itself disturb the Ho state.

concerns.quote: The reading method also appears intrinsically invasive. The reading relies on strong tip-atom interactions, including strong magnetic fields from the Co-functionalized tip and the scattering electrons from the tip apex.
concerns.summary: Force readout may perturb the spin through tip fields and electron scattering, and the observed lifetime of several seconds is no better than current-based readout.

concerns.quote: While the authors argue that electrical currents lead to Joule heating, this effect on reading and writing atoms is typically negligible under standard STM operating conditions
concerns.summary: The Joule-heating motivation for avoiding current is weak, because heating is negligible in standard STM operation.

concerns.quote: changes in the tip apex configuration are likely during readout. If so, it could make it difficult to reliably distinguish the two Ho spin states
concerns.summary: At near- or beyond-contact distances, tip apex changes could mimic or obscure the frequency-shift contrast attributed to spin states.

concerns.quote: A short vertical decay does not necessarily imply narrow lateral control, particularly for mechanically mediated interactions and magnetic stray fields.
concerns.summary: The claim of more spatially localized switching rests on vertical decay of the switching rate (Fig. 4c), which does not establish lateral addressability.

concerns.quote: Adachi and colleagues use magnetic tips and oscillations amplitudes of 65 pm that could randomize the states via Landau Zener tunneling, as the motion of a magnetic field is akin to performing magnetic field sweeps
concerns.summary: The oscillating magnetic tip could sweep the local field through hyperfine-induced level crossings and cause Landau-Zener switching rather than force-based switching, and this is not discussed.

concerns.quote: the authors must demonstrate reversible state control using a nonmagnetic tip
concerns.summary: To isolate force-based writing, switching should be performed with a nonmagnetic tip and the state then read magnetically.

concerns.quote: exclude magnetic-field–induced transitions via quantitative modeling of the tip field
concerns.summary: A quantitative model of the tip's magnetic field is needed to rule out field-induced transitions.

concerns.quote: provide external-field and hyperfine-resolved switching statistics
concerns.summary: Switching statistics as a function of external field, resolved by hyperfine state, are missing, and no field dependence is shown.

concerns.quote: substantial experimental evidence is relayed to the supplement. We believe that all major claims need to be sufficiently corroborated within the main part of the article already.
concerns.summary: Key evidence for the main claims sits in the supplement rather than the main text.

concerns.quote: no justification given for the choice of 3T magnetic biasing field
concerns.summary: The choice of a 3 T bias field is not justified.

concerns.quote: Ho adatoms would not be stable at zero field without hyperfine interaction, which is not addressed by Adachi
concerns.summary: The role of the hyperfine interaction in Ho stability, including at zero field, is not discussed.

concerns.quote: oscillation amplitude only cited in figure captions and not in experimental section
concerns.summary: The oscillation amplitude should be stated in the experimental description.

concerns.quote: using 120mV to monitor Ho state could already lead to current induced state reversal
concerns.summary: 120 mV exceeds the known electronic switching threshold, so state preparation and monitoring at this bias could itself cause current-induced reversal.

concerns.quote: Adachi and coworkers mention “exceeding threshold” for instance on p1L68 but do not clarify what parameters they are referring to.
concerns.summary: It is unclear which parameter the 'threshold' for switching refers to.

concerns.quote: Fig 4. Redundant panels (a) and (b)
concerns.summary: Fig. 4a and 4b show redundant telegraph traces.

concerns.quote: no mention of exchange and dipolar magnetic fields created by the cobalt functionalized tip
concerns.summary: The exchange and dipolar fields from the Co tip acting on the Ho atom are not considered.

concerns.quote: missing switching histogram that should reveal state preference for Ho state aligned with external magnetic field
concerns.summary: A histogram of state populations is needed to show the expected preference for the field-aligned state.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: no discussion of energetics Ho state aligned with magnetic field has a meV preference to the opposite state
concerns.summary: The meV-scale Zeeman energy preference of the field-aligned state is not discussed.

concerns.quote: Stevens parameters from SI differ from cited parameters for J=8
concerns.summary: The crystal-field Stevens parameters in the SI are inconsistent with literature values for J = 8.

later_concerns.quote: Does Fig. 4a correspond to the reading or writing process? If it is a reading, the lifetime is only several seconds
later_concerns.summary: R2 asks whether Fig. 4a shows reading or writing, requests readout and writing traces side by side, and asks for the longest achievable readout lifetime.
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

later_concerns.quote: The statement that “In this near-contact regime, electron scattering from the tip apex is suppressed.” may be incorrect.
later_concerns.summary: Electron scattering grows exponentially as the tip approaches, so the readout may be invasive, contrary to a statement added in revision.

later_concerns.quote: The statement that 3T is far from the hyperfine levels is misleading... exchange forces dominate and have been shown to easily exceed 3T
later_concerns.summary: Near point contact, tip exchange fields can greatly change the effective field on Ho, so the 3 T argument does not rule out Landau-Zener switching.

later_concerns.quote: The authors could repeat the experiment at zero field... Alternatively, repeat the experiment at even more extreme fields and investigate whether the switching dynamics is field dependent.
later_concerns.summary: R3 proposes zero-field or higher-field experiments to separate force-driven from field-driven switching, after the nonmagnetic-tip control was dismissed.

later_concerns.quote: this is not necessarily a unique feature of a supposed force based reversal as the field-sweep technique introduced by Forrester Phys. Rev. B 100, 180405(R) (2019) already covers non conducting substrates.
later_concerns.summary: The claimed advantage for insulating substrates is not unique, because a noninvasive field-sweep method already works there.

later_concerns.quote: at such a short tip-atom distance, the tip field arising from exchange interaction is expected to dominate over the dipolar stray field.
later_concerns.summary: The SI argument treats the tip field as a dipolar stray field, but the oscillating exchange field should be discussed as a possible switching driver.
